themes_detail.label: Lead contamination surge
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints spiked to 4 this week compared to a 0.4-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—signaling a potential environmental health crisis in Fordham/University Heights that demands immediate investigation into sources and affected buildings.
evidence: 4 lead complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49, severity: high)
This represents a 967% spike in a single week, indicating a sudden emergence rather than long-running issue
Lead exposure poses serious health risks, especially for children and pregnant women in the district
reporting_angles: Investigate which buildings or properties triggered the spike—are they clustered geographically or by age/condition?
Interview NYC Health Dept and HPD on whether they've identified a source (water system, building materials, renovation work) and what remediation is underway
Speak with residents in affected buildings about exposure risks and what support they're receiving

themes_detail.label: Sewer system deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints reached 9 this week versus a 3.6-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 148% spike (z-score: 3.6)—indicating potential infrastructure failure or blockage affecting multiple blocks in the district.
evidence: 9 sewer complaints filed this week vs. 3.6-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.6, severity: high)
148% increase suggests acute infrastructure problem, not gradual deterioration
Sewer failures can lead to sewage backup, property damage, and public health hazards
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if there's a known sewer break, blockage, or overflow event in the district this week
Map the 9 complaints geographically to identify if they cluster on specific blocks or are spread across the district
Interview affected residents about backups, odors, or other symptoms; follow up on repair timelines

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team activity spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints surged to 4 this week from a 0.4-per-week average—a 1,167% increase (z-score: 9.04)—sustained over 4 weeks, suggesting a targeted enforcement campaign or emerging compliance crisis in specific buildings.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints this week vs. 0.4-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.04, severity: medium)
1,167% spike sustained over a 4-week period indicates ongoing enforcement action, not a one-time anomaly
SPIT is triggered by serious HPD violations (heat, plumbing, electrical) requiring city intervention
reporting_angles: Request HPD records to identify which buildings triggered SPIT involvement and what violations were cited
Interview HPD about whether a particular landlord or building class is under systematic inspection
Speak with affected tenants about living conditions, notice of violations, and remediation status

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk deterioration spreading
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints reached 7 two weeks ago—a 211% spike from a 2.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 3.41)—suggesting concentrated pavement failure or recent storm damage affecting pedestrian safety across multiple blocks.
evidence: 7 sidewalk condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.41, severity: high)
211% spike indicates acute, geographically concentrated problem rather than baseline deterioration
Poor sidewalk conditions create tripping hazards and liability for elderly and disabled residents
reporting_angles: Map the 7 complaints to identify which blocks are most affected and whether there's a common cause (recent flooding, utility work, aging infrastructure)
Contact NYC DOT about repair schedules and whether the district is prioritized for sidewalk reconstruction
Canvass affected blocks for visual confirmation and interview residents about hazards and injury risk

themes_detail.label: Encampment growth in district
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints reached 16 three weeks ago—a 113% increase from a 7.5-per-week baseline (z-score: 2.45)—indicating a growing visible homelessness presence that may reflect broader citywide trends or district-specific service gaps.
evidence: 16 encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.5-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.45, severity: medium)
113% spike over a 3-week window indicates acceleration rather than isolated incidents
Encampments affect public space access, sanitation, and community perception of safety
reporting_angles: Interview DHS and NYPD about whether encampments are concentrated in specific parks, streets, or transit hubs and why enforcement/outreach has not contained them
Speak with business owners and residents about quality-of-life impacts and whether city services (sanitation, outreach) are responsive
Profile individuals living in encampments to understand barriers to shelter access and whether district-level service gaps exist
